[[File:Venice Revealed_poster.jpg|thumb|250px|''Venice Revealed'' poster]]
'''''Venice Revealed''''' (French: ''Venice Révélée'') was an interactive exhibition  developed as a collaborative partnership between the [https://grandpalais-immersif.fr Grand Palais Immersif], the {{Wiki|Fondazione Musei Civici di Venezia}}, [https://iconem.com ICONEM], and [[Ubisoft]], using the [[Venice|city]]'s models from ''[[Assassin's Creed II]]'' for visualization. It ran from 21 September 2022 to 19 February 2023.<ref>{{Cite web| url=https://grandpalais-immersif.fr/en/venice-revealed|title=Venice Revealed| publisher=''Grand Palais Immersif''| date=29 September 2022| accessdate=27 April 2023}}</ref>

==Publisher's summary==
''[[Renaissance]] [[Venice]] in the world of'' [[Assassin's Creed (series)|Assassin’s Creed]]''. Take a unique journey to late 15th century Venice (1481), an experience from the world of the video game'' Assassin’s Creed II''. By bringing to life detailed reconstructions of cities, monuments and past civilisations,'' Assassin's Creed ''offers a gateway to history for millions of gamers around the world.''

''Ubisoft and Grand Palais Immersif have joined forces to offer you an immersion in the glorious past of Venice during the Renaissance, thanks to interactive videos accompanied by magnificent concept art.''

''In this room, you follow [[Ezio Auditore da Firenze|Ezio]], the famous video game hero, through four {{Wiki|Sestiere|sestieri}} or emblematic districts of Venice: [[Castello District|Castello]], [[Dorsoduro]], [[San Marco District, Venice|San Marco]], and [[San Polo District|San Polo]]. [[Freerunning|Climb]] to the top of the city’s towers, walk along the {{Wiki|Venetian Lagoon|lagoon}}, discover the wooden [[Ponte di Rialto|Rialto Bridge]], and infiltrate a [[Carnevale|colourful masked ball]].''<ref>{{Cite web| url=https://grandpalais-immersif.fr/sites/immersif/files/documents/Venise_Guide_EN.pdf| title=Venice Revealed, an immersive exhibition | publisher=Grand Palais Immersif| accessdate=27 April 2023}}</ref>
